key_insight: A multimodal cardiac foundation model pretrained on signals and clinician text from 1.7M people learns device- and setting-agnostic representations that deliver accurate, reliable cardiac assessments across hospital ECGs and consumer wearable recordings.
problem_solved: Bridges domain gaps between clinical-grade and consumer cardiac data by creating a single pretrained model that generalizes across devices, signal qualities, and care settings, reducing the need for device-specific retraining and fragmented pipelines.
method: Large-scale multimodal pretraining on 1.7 million individuals combining raw heart signals (ECG/PPG) with textual clinical interpretations to learn unified embeddings.
Foundation-model architecture (signal encoders + text encoder → joint embedding space) enabling transfer, zero-/few-shot adaptation, and calibration across device types and recording settings.
Extensive cross-device, cross-scenario evaluation demonstrating robustness, reliability, and clinical-level performance on both hospital ECGs and at‑home wearable data.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to build device‑agnostic cardiac tools with less labeled data and faster deployment across clinical and consumer settings, improving scalability and real-world reliability of cardiac AI.

paper_title: Cardiac health assessment across scenarios and devices using a multimodal foundation model pretrained on data from 1.7 million individuals
paper_authors: Xiao Gu, Wei Tang, Jinpei Han, Veer Sangha, Fenglin Liu
